critique.good: All terms stay on one line, making the shaded identifier column easy to scan. Definitions and examples have reasonably similar line counts, so most rows read as connected units.
critique.problems: The term column has substantial unused space beneath and beside short labels. Examples are frequently broken into short lines, while several definitions remain dense.
critique.cause: The 156px term column preserves every label but consumes space that could improve the 163px example column or the 245px definition column.

critique.good: The wider examples read comfortably, with natural phrase lengths. The narrower term column still distinguishes row labels clearly.
critique.problems: Definitions form tall, narrow blocks, especially for eventual consistency and CAP theorem. The shorter examples leave large blank areas beside them, weakening the visual connection across rows. Two term labels wrap.
critique.cause: The 234px example column receives more width than the 210px definition column, although definitions contain considerably more prose. The 120px term column also cannot accommodate every label on one line.

critique.good: Definitions have comfortable line lengths, and the compact term column leaves more space for prose. No technical words split mid-word, and the shorter overall table makes comparison easier.
critique.problems: Examples become narrow stacks of short lines and often determine row height, leaving blank space under their companion definitions. Several term labels wrap, including Circuit breaker and Write-ahead log, reducing scanability.
critique.cause: The 300px definition column leaves only 156px for examples and 108px for terms. Those widths favor definitions too strongly for the paired reading task.

critique.good: The term column is easy to scan, and the definition and example read clearly across each row. The rows have a consistent rhythm, with no mid-word splits.
critique.problems: Eventual consistency and Write-ahead log wrap, while several examples have short, ragged lines and leave space below them beside longer definitions.
critique.cause: The 120px term column is too narrow for those labels. The 174px example column gives the examples noticeably shorter lines than the 270px definition column.

critique.good: The wider term column keeps Write-ahead log on one line and makes the row identifiers easy to pick out. Examples remain legible, and no words split mid-word.
critique.problems: Eventual consistency still wraps, while several definitions gain lines and the final row becomes especially tall. The extra width in the term column produces a less balanced distribution of space.
critique.cause: Increasing Term to 135px reduces Definition to 255px without making the longest term fit on one line. That narrower definition measure creates additional wrapping.

critique.good: The wider example column improves line length and gives the two prose columns a more balanced appearance. Definitions retain the same measure and row heights as in r1A, with no mid-word splits.
critique.problems: The term column feels cramped: Circuit breaker joins Eventual consistency and Write-ahead log in wrapping. The narrowest single-word label nearly fills its cell, weakening the ease of scanning the identifiers.
critique.cause: At 108px, Term leaves only 87px for text. Moving those 12px to Example improves its measure but makes more term labels wrap.

critique.good: The term column is easy to scan, and the definition and example read as companion passages. The rows have a steady rhythm, with no broken technical words.
critique.problems: Eventual consistency and Write-ahead log wrap in the term column. The example for Circuit breaker is more tightly set than the adjacent definition, while some shorter examples leave space below.
critique.cause: The 116px term width leaves 95px for text; the 178px example width leaves 157px. The latter is adequate overall but constrains some longer examples.

critique.good: The wider definition column gives several explanations comfortable line lengths, and the term labels remain distinct.
critique.problems: The examples become visibly narrow and fragmented. Eventual consistency and Circuit breaker grow taller because their examples take six lines, weakening the otherwise regular row rhythm.
critique.cause: The 164px example column leaves only 143px for text, while the 280px definition column receives space that does not consistently reduce row heights.

critique.good: The wider examples read more naturally than in r2B, and the prose columns have a balanced relationship. Rows retain the same steady heights as r2A, with no mid-word splits.
critique.problems: The term labels Eventual consistency and Write-ahead log still wrap. Some definitions, especially CAP theorem, remain dense, so taking much more space from the definition column could upset the balance.
critique.cause: The 120px term column leaves 99px for text, while the 260px definition column leaves 239px. The example column receives 184px, improving its wrapping at the expense of definition width.

understanding.purpose: Help readers understand distributed-systems terms through definitions and examples.
understanding.reading: Readers scan the first column for a term, then read across the row to connect its definition with an example; they may also compare definitions or examples down a column.
groups: Definition and Example are companion prose columns: one explains the concept and the other illustrates it.
Term is the row identifier and should remain easy to scan independently.
may_wrap: Definitions and examples at natural word boundaries
Multiword terms when needed; their wrapping can fit within the height created by longer prose

bad.why: The term column would have substantial unused space in most rows, while the definition column would be compressed despite carrying the most text. This would produce longer, more fragmented definitions and weaken the rhythm between rows.

contrast.why: The term column would have substantial unused space in most rows, while the definition column would be compressed despite carrying the most text. This would produce longer, more fragmented definitions and weaken the rhythm between rows.

final.rationale: r3A gives the definition the most room while leaving examples wide enough to read comfortably. Its term column keeps “Circuit breaker” on one line, and the two longer labels wrap at word boundaries. The six equally tall middle rows make it easy to scan across from a term to its definition and example.

general: Allocate width according to each column’s role and text, while preserving enough room for row labels to support scanning.
Judge wrapping across the whole row: a gain in one column can create more awkward breaks or extra height in another.
specific: The definitions carry substantially more text than the examples, so they merit the widest column.
A term width near 116 px keeps “Circuit breaker” on one line, though “Eventual consistency” and “Write-ahead log” still wrap.

final.tradeoffs: r2A gives definitions slightly more room; r2C gives terms slightly more room. r3B keeps every term on one line, but its narrower definitions wrap more and create taller rows.
final.uncertain: The ranges are approximate, based on the rendered candidates, and are not guarantees for every interpolated width. A designer who values single-line term labels more highly might prefer r3B despite its taller rows.

A.why: The equal-width columns give the short terms too much space and squeeze the longer definitions into many short lines, making rows unnecessarily tall.

B.why: The generous definition column supports fluent reading, but several row labels wrap, including Circuit breaker and Write-ahead log.

C.why: The columns give definitions ample room while keeping all but the longest term on one line. Examples remain readable and the rows hold together well.

D.why: Definition and example widths are well balanced, though Eventual consistency and Write-ahead log wrap in the term column.

E.why: Definitions and examples read comfortably, but the narrow term column wraps three labels, weakening the glossary's scanability.

F.why: All terms stay on one line, but their wide column leaves definitions somewhat cramped and produces tall rows with unused space beside them.

reviews.unsure: C trades some definition width for more intact row labels; D is a close alternative if compactness is preferred.

A.why: The definition has room to read comfortably, examples remain clear, and only two multiword terms wrap. The rows stay easy to scan across.

B.why: All terms fit on one line, but the wide term column leaves substantial empty space while definitions wrap into many short lines.

C.why: Definitions and examples have comfortable widths, but the narrow term column wraps three labels, including Circuit breaker.

D.why: Most terms stay on one line and both prose columns remain readable. Definitions wrap a little more than in A, making some rows taller.

E.why: The prose columns are well proportioned and rows read clearly, though three term labels wrap in the narrow first column.

F.why: The wide term column keeps labels intact but leaves large blank areas. The narrow definition column produces long stacks of short lines and tall rows.

reviews.unsure: D is a plausible alternative if keeping more term labels on one line is valued more highly than giving the definitions extra width.
